title: Weather, nature & seasons
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons, describe the natural world, and say what is about to happen ('it's going to rain').
intro: Tamil Nadu is hot most of the year — Chennai jokes that it has three seasons: hot, hotter and hottest — and gets most of its rain from the **north-east monsoon** in October–December. Tamil weather expressions use specific verbs: rain **falls** (பெய்), the sun **beats** (அடி), wind **blows** (அடி / வீசு).

vocab.note: மழை பெய்யுது 'it's raining'; past பெஞ்சுது penjudu

phrases.en: It's very hot and sunny today.
It looks like it's going to rain.
It gets very cold in Ooty.
Apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow.
There's been little rain this year.

grammar.title: Weather expressions
grammar.body:
Weather uses specific noun + verb pairs, usually in the neuter (-உது / -உம்) form:

**மழை பெய்யுது** — rain is falling (it's raining)
**வெயில் அடிக்குது** — the sun is beating (it's hot and sunny)
**காத்து அடிக்குது / வீசுது** — wind is blowing
**குளிருது** — it's cold (lit. it chills)
**இடி இடிக்குது** — it's thundering
**வேர்க்குது** — (I'm) sweating

For a state, use **-ஆ இருக்கு**: சூடா இருக்கு 'it's hot', குளிரா இருக்கு 'it's cold', மேகமா இருக்கு 'it's cloudy'. The neuter future **-உம்** expresses general truths: சென்னையில மே மாசம் ரொம்ப வெயில் அடிக்கும் 'In Chennai it's very hot in May'.

examples.en: It's cold in the month of Margazhi.
There's always a good breeze on the beach.

grammar.title: 'It's going to…': -ப் போகுது, மாதிரி இருக்கு, and -ஆம் (hearsay)
grammar.body:
To say something **is about to happen**, use the infinitive + **போ** 'go' in the present: **மழை பெய்யப் போகுது** 'it's going to rain', **நான் சாப்பிடப் போறேன்** 'I'm going to eat'. This is the Tamil 'going to'.

To say something **looks like** it will happen, use the relative participle + **மாதிரி இருக்கு** 'it's like': மழை வர்ற மாதிரி இருக்கு 'it looks like rain'.

A handy spoken suffix: **-ஆம்** *-ām* on a verb means 'reportedly / they say': புயல் வருமாம் 'apparently a cyclone will come', மழை பெய்யுமாம் 'they say it'll rain'.

examples.en: It's gone dark — it's going to rain.
The bus is about to leave, come quickly!
It looks like it'll be sunny today.

dialogue.title: A cyclone warning
dialogue.setting: Meena and her neighbour Sarah chat on the terrace in November.

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: ஆமா, நாளைக்குப் புயல் வருமாம். டிவில சொன்னாங்க.
lines.roman: āmā, nāḷaikkup puyal varumām. ṭīvila sonnānga.
lines.en: Yes, apparently a cyclone is coming tomorrow. They said so on TV.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Oh no! Is it a very big cyclone?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.en: I don't know. But they say there'll be a lot of rain.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Does it always rain like this in Chennai?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: இல்ல, மழைக்காலத்துல மட்டும். மத்த மாசம் எல்லாம் வெயில்தான்!
lines.roman: illa, maḻaikkālattula maṭṭum. matta māsam ellām veyildān!
lines.en: No, only in the rainy season. All the other months it's just sun!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Will the office be open tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Meena
lines.native: லீவு விடுவாங்கன்னு நினைக்கிறேன். தண்ணி, மெழுகுவர்த்தி எல்லாம் வாங்கி வைங்க.
lines.roman: līvu viḍuvāngannu ninaikkirēn. taṇṇi, meḻuguvartti ellām vāngi vainga.
lines.en: I think they'll declare a holiday. Buy and keep water, candles and so on.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: சரி. இப்போவே மழை பெய்யப் போகுது, உள்ள போலாம்!
lines.roman: sari. ippōvē maḻai peyyap pōgudu, uḷḷa pōlām!
lines.en: OK. It's about to rain right now — let's go inside!

culture: Classical Tamil poetry divides the land into five landscapes (திணை *tiṇai*) — mountains, forest, farmland, seashore and desert — each linked to a mood of love. Today, people in hot Tamil Nadu welcome rain joyfully, and the cool month of **Margazhi** (mid-December–mid-January) is Chennai's famous music and dance season.
